With 32 negatives, candidate CE is −log[exp(s⁺/τ)/(exp(s⁺/τ)+Σ₃₂exp(s⁻/τ))]: competition among 33 candidates, not full-catalog likelihood. Uniform sampling does not make the uncorrected denominator a full-softmax estimate. For 32 unique negatives from an eligible pool of M items, an importance-weighted partition estimate retains exp(s⁺/τ) and multiplies the negative sum by M/32; its log remains biased at finite sample size. Excluding training positives also changes the target support; zero-probability excluded items cannot be recovered by correction. [Candidate-sampling reference](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf), [sampled-softmax analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a/blanc18a.pdf).

 gSASRec instead uses independent sigmoid terms: −[β log σ(s⁺)+Σₖ log(1−σ(s⁻))]/(k+1), with α=k/(|I|−1), β=1−t+tα. Thus t=0 gives BCE; t=1 supplies the paper’s calibration correction under its sampling assumptions. This is neither categorical normalization nor temperature scaling. gSASRec changes both loss and negative count, so gains cannot automatically be attributed to gBCE. [Official implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec).

Recommended controls: compare BCE, gBCE and candidate CE using identical 32-negative draws, exclusions, score parameterization, seeds and training budget; separately vary k. Fix τ=1 first, then tune temperature separately from t. Report proposal/inclusion probabilities and correction choices. Exclude padding, the target and known training positives; unobserved items can still be false negatives. Implement exclusions inside the sampler while user IDs are available, preserving the downstream tensor-only batch contract. Alternatively carry user IDs alongside batches for loss-time sampling. Truncated sequences cannot reliably identify users or reconstruct complete training histories; never consult held-out labels.
